_doc: Worked example of one JBEQ-MDM fact sheet, the input scripts/jbeq_decide.py decide() reads. Full field documentation lives in the module docstring at the top of scripts/jbeq_decide.py. A real fact-sheets.json file passed to the CLI is a JSON object of {"CASE-ID": {fact sheet, without this _doc key}, ...}; this file shows one entry's shape plus four worked variants below it so the same file demonstrates the rules that fire on real cases. Round 5 (2026-09-06) grew the schema with the identity-kind fields (object_type_a/object_type_b, lifecycle, requested_action, requested_relation_type, authoritative_identifier, contradicted_attributes, distinct_operational_attributes, location_comparison, effective_dates); every example below carries them at a value that does not change which rule fires, so each example still demonstrates only the one rule its name and _comment say. Round 6 (2026-09-06) added one further OPTIONAL key, requested_parent (string or null, absent from every example below): the entity a request asks to become the parent, read only when requested_relation_type matches a stated hierarchy TYPE but the input asks to reverse which side is the PARENT (see scripts/jbeq_decide.py's module docstring and rule link_vs_reject). Round 7 (2026-09-06, per ~/.claude/evidence/review-u1-2026-09-06.md section F and FIX-DIRECTIVE-2026-09-06.md section 15) widened requested_action's enum to match_on_stated_basis and record_write (no rule gates on either value yet: this widening is a schema-and-prompt-only second pass, pending a fresh re-extraction of the frozen 70 before anything reads it) and added one new location_comparison value, same_area_renamed, which rule L DOES already read, exactly like notation_variant_only.

_enums._doc: One source of truth for every closed-vocabulary field decide() and validate() enforce (round 5 repair, 2026-09-06, closing the L12 gap the design review found: validate used to check key presence only, never value membership, so 20 of 45 round 5 sheets carried off-enum free text in stated_relation and stated_difference that matched no rule and silently fell to the default). Read by scripts/jbeq_decide.py's _load_enums(). identifier domain and identifier status are deliberately NOT enumerated here: the real fact sheets already carry many legitimate domain-like values (crm_guid, customer_code, site_id, store_id and more) far beyond the five illustrative values named in the module docstring, so treating that field as closed would refuse sheets for a reason unrelated to this repair. tenant_boundary is a two-value field decide() does not branch on for anything this repair touches, and is left unenforced for the same reason: this list enforces exactly the fields the design review named as load-bearing for the L12 fix, not every field that happens to have a small value set.

example_rule_5_keep_separate._comment: Same address only, one side a one-to-many consolidation point: boundary rule 5 fires KEEP SEPARATE.

example_rule_C_reject_match._comment: A candidate crosses a stated tenant wall: boundary rule C fires REJECT MATCH before any merge ladder runs.

example_rule_B_weak_escalate._comment: A 0.83 name-match score only, no corporate number, an irreversible delete: boundary rule B fires ESCALATE, never a merge, because evidence_strength is weak.

example_rule_D_hierarchy_keep_separate._comment: Capital parent, trade-flow parent and reporting parent all valid and different: boundary rule D fires KEEP SEPARATE, since the three hierarchy types are independent and none of them conflicts with another.

example_rule_A_blank_field_escalate._comment: A prefecture field is blank, but the banchi and postal code corroborate without confirming: boundary rule A fires ESCALATE, not NO-DATA.

example_rule_r_authoritative_identifier_._comment: authoritative_identifier=conflicting covers TWO shapes, not only two different valid identifiers disagreeing outright: (1) a reused identifier now pointing at a different entity than the one it used to identify (lifecycle=identifier_reused on the side that reused it), and (2) two identifiers that carry the SAME value but in different domains, which decide()'s rule_r reads as a conflict on its own even when authoritative_identifier itself is left aligned. authoritative_identifier=absent means no authoritative identifier is available on EITHER side, never merely that the two sides disagree. This example shows shape (1): a corporate number the input states was reused after the original holder dissolved, now naming an unrelated successor entity. With a proposal on record (requested_action=match_on_stated_basis), rule_r fires REJECT MATCH via gated_reject; without one, the identical facts would answer KEEP SEPARATE instead (review-u1-2026-09-06.md section A).
